title: COPing with and CAring for Infants with special Needs (COPCA®) versus Usual Care in Germany (UCD): A feasibility study with process evaluation
summary:
Background: Worldwide, approximately 7.5% of children under 5 are affected by developmental disorders. Cerebral palsy (CP) – one of the most common neurodevelopmental conditions – is typically not diagnosed until after 18 months of age, as the brain is still rapidly developing during this period. Early identification and support for at-risk infants is therefore crucial. Research consistently shows that early interventions combining playful, everyday challenges with active family involvement produce the best outcomes.
In Germany, Bobath-based therapy is the legally mandated standard approach – despite limited evidence of its effectiveness for children with CP. In this model, therapists lead the exercises and instruct parents directly. A newer programme called COPCA® (Coping with and Caring for infants with special needs) takes a different approach: parents are included as equal partners, coached rather than instructed, and encouraged to support their child's motor development independently in everyday life. Early studies from Switzerland and the Netherlands have shown promising results for COPCA®, including better motor development and improved quality of life. To date, no comparable studies exist in the German healthcare context.
Research question: Is a larger comparative study between COPCA® and usual clinical practice (UCD) feasible within the German healthcare system? And can the two therapeutic approaches be meaningfully distinguished from one another in practice?
Methods: Twelve families with infants aged 3–15 months at elevated risk for neurodevelopmental disorders participate in the study. Six families receive COPCA®, six receive usual physiotherapy (UCD). The intervention lasts 3 months. Children's motor development is assessed at baseline and post-intervention using a standardised observational instrument (IMP). At 2.5 months, one therapy session per family is video-recorded and analysed to compare the content of the two approaches. Parents also complete a questionnaire on satisfaction and self-efficacy (FOEI). Results will determine whether a larger follow-up trial is justified and feasible.
conditions: Children aged 3–15 months with a Total IMP Score ≤ 15% and/or Performance ≤ 15% and/or Variation ≤ 15% (≙ risk of a neuromotor developmental disorder)

interventions.name:
Duration of intervention: 3 months
a) COPCA®
Family-centred coaching using specific coaching and neuromotor strategies, promoting self-initiated motor activity, carried out in a home or clinical setting, with duration and frequency tailored to individual needs and documented by a COPCA® coach in a

b) UCD: 
Therapist-led sessions involving direct instruction and demonstration, specific motor exercises, usually in a clinical setting, lasting approx. 45–60 minutes; conducted by certified paediatric Bobath therapists, usually once or twice a week

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• With a total IMP score ≤ 15 % and/or performance ≤ 15 % and/or variation ≤ 15 % (≙ risk of a neuromotor developmental disorder (NME))
• Consent for video and questionnaire)
Exclusion criteria:
• severe congenital abnormalities
• severe sensory impairments
